caption: What if you could turn anything into gold? The recipe is simple: lead has 82 protons and gold has 79, so knock out 3 protons (and at least one neutron) and lead becomes gold. In 2025, CERN scientists showed the Large Hadron Collider really does this, when lead atoms zoom past each other in near misses. From 2015 to 2018 it made about 86 billion gold atoms, weighing just 29 picograms, and each one broke apart in a tiny fraction of a second. At that speed, one gram would take longer than the age of the universe. Nature does it better: gold can be forged when neutron stars crash, and one crash seen in 2017 may have made an Earth's worth. All the gold ever mined, about 224,000 tonnes, would fit in a cube about 23 metres wide, and Indian homes hold up to 25,000 tonnes of it. What would YOU turn into gold? 👇
